adjudication_of_control_screened.note: Hand-read all 9. Roughly 3-4 are genuinely valid directed claims - about the SAME ~1/3 survival rate as the real run's 5/15.

valid.why: 'Erythropoietin drives breast cancer progression by activation of its receptor EPOR' - a clean, valid driver claim, from a RANDOM pairing.
'OPRK1 drives ... neuroendocrine prostate cancer' - directed and asserted.
'IFNa activates TYK2/STAT/HSPA5 signaling to promote NSCLC proliferation and metastasis'.

weak_or_false.why: ENTITY COLLISION. Sentence is about beta-2 adrenergic receptor (b2-AR); graph 'AR' is the ANDROGEN receptor. Distinct bug.
'promoter CpG island' methylation - the 'promoter' pattern again, no driver predicate.
'ERBB4 promoter DNA methylation' - same promoter artifact.
MMP1 is downstream of PRKRA, not the asserted subject.
MAP2K2 is a mid-axis member; subject is YTHDF2.
Part of a circRNA/miRNA axis; indirect.

conclusion: Post-hoc PubMed grounding carries essentially NO information about whether the graph's proposal was correct. Randomly scrambled protein-disease pairs ground at a statistically indistinguishable rate (7.5% vs 12.5%, p=0.28) AND at comparable adjudicated quality (~1/3 valid in both arms). This does NOT mean the discovered edges are false - EPOR really does drive breast cancer. It means the PROPOSAL step added no measurable signal: you would find about as many true edges by picking pairs at random. The pipeline is literature mining, not prediction validation, and must not be described as the latter.
